answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the nadir schedule in the tide ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the timber checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 159 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 8 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
